newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise in calm market, await Fed.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise in calm market, await Fed.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Monday after a calm session in which players edged towards the conviction that the market has discounted a possible hike in U.S. rates.
"It is very possible that the market has now discounted a hike in the U.S.," said a trader at a local brokerage house.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets Tuesday.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 5/8 to 90-7/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.30 to 127.00.
"The market was just waiting," said another trader, pointing to the thin activity as players stayed on the sidelines in anticipation of news from the Federal Reserve.

Traders and analysts said the biggest surprise element for the market would be if the Federal Reserve did nothing at Tuesday's meeting. No action could raise fears that monetary policy will have to be tightened more later in the year.
But whatever happens, traders said the anticipated upgrade in Argentina's credit rating could very well outweigh any negative news from the U.S.
Call money rates fell to 5.80 percent from 5.88 percent.
